records.notes: Inputs are assumptions. Same benefit cannot be counted in two pilots.

public_checks: Pilot costing INR 2 lakh once plus INR 0.6 lakh/year with INR 1.8 lakh/year realized benefit has INR 1.2 lakh annual net benefit and 20-month simple payback, assuming steady benefit from day one.
Portfolio respects budget and prevents double-counting the same hours/revenue across pilots.
Low adoption or failed quality threshold causes an explicit revise/stop decision.
starting_state.limit: Small teaching fixture for a bounded prototype. Market demand, willingness to pay and production performance remain unproven.

extension._label: TEAM-AUTHORED ASSUMPTIONS. Not part of the C23 fixture. Synthetic, illustrative, unproven.

parse_rules.period_rule: recurring amounts (savings, running cost, balance-sheet lines) are annualised from the period their column header names; one-time setup is never annualised
parse_rules.possible_duplicate_rule: different ids with the same task (case-insensitive), setup, benefit and running cost

advice_rules.fixture_cap_rule: fixture (synthetic) money values cap the evidence band at Low

NET_NOT_POSITIVE.action: re-scope the pilot: remove one cost line or grow the benefit before it is proposed again

NON_CASHABLE.action: restate the benefit with a cash line (budget line, invoice reduction) instead of capacity value
NON_CASHABLE.expected_test: benefit type with cash factor 1.0 and a stated cash line

FIXTURE_ONLY_EVIDENCE.action: replace one fixture number with a real one: an invoice-based recurring cost line or a benefit driver from real volumes
FIXTURE_ONLY_EVIDENCE.expected_test: no decision-driving input sourced from the fixture

MONEY_ASSUMED.action: back one money figure with an invoice, a signed contract or a written vendor quote
MONEY_ASSUMED.expected_test: a decision-driving money input sourced as observed

NO_OBSERVED_ADOPTION.action: run one adoption spot-check batch over the real users
NO_OBSERVED_ADOPTION.expected_test: observed adoption recorded from the batch

NO_OBSERVED_QUALITY.action: run one quality spot-check on pilot outputs and record it
NO_OBSERVED_QUALITY.expected_test: observed quality recorded from the batch

RUN_COST_ASSUMED.action: get written vendor pricing or an invoice trail for the AI running cost
RUN_COST_ASSUMED.expected_test: a recurring-cost line replaces the 20%-of-setup assumption

ADOPTION_ASSUMED.action: schedule an adoption measurement for week 1-2 of any stage

LOW_OBSERVED_ADOPTION.expected_test: observed adoption >= break-even adoption after the experiment

LOW_READINESS.expected_test: readiness at medium or higher before funding

BREAK_EVEN_BEYOND_HORIZON.action: re-cost with a faster ramp (build and rollout sooner) or re-decide at the next budget cycle

CONSERVATIVE_DIES.action: fund from the training/capacity budget instead of the savings ledger, or convert the benefit to cash

compare_rules.drop_rule: net annual savings <= 0 or break-even beyond the horizon
compare_rules.selector: highest total net annual benefit within budget, overlap counted once

economics_rules.competitiveness_ratio: annualised AI cost ÷ gross benefit, or AI cost per unit ÷ human cost per unit when the baseline gives volume and per-unit human cost

budget_checks.first_year_inr: setup + first-12-month running cost ≤ first-year budget
budget_checks.total_inr: (setup + running cost over the horizon) × (1 + contingency) ≤ total budget

economics_rules.at_risk_rule: fits without contingency but not with it (total), or uses more than 90% of a line

tier_modes.graduated: each unit pays its own tier's price
tier_modes.volume: every unit pays the price of the tier the total falls in

pricing_rules.package_rule: cheapest mix of whole packages (plus overage, if priced) that covers the month's units

forecast.selection: lowest hold-out MAPE; ties by method order
forecast.fallback: assumed_growth_fallback: last known usage × (1 + annual growth)^(m/12), labelled

pricing_rules.optimiser: plan with the lowest base-scenario annual cost; also reports the plan with the lowest worst-case (high-scenario) cost and the regret of each plan

rules: reject: net annual benefit <= 0 and a running-cost cut of more than 30% would be needed, or no part of the benefit is cashable
renegotiate: net <= 0 but a running-cost cut of at most 30% makes it positive, or the cost competitiveness class is uncompetitive
defer: break-even beyond the horizon, or the proposal is over budget
gather_evidence: no decision-driving input is observed or calculated
limited_pilot: evidence band low, data readiness not ready, or competitiveness marginal
invest: every gate passes with evidence band medium or high
decision_rules.ranking_scale: each criterion min-max normalised to 0-100 across the compared set (all equal = 100); score = Σ weight × normalised; ties follow the 6-tier order
data_readiness_checks: team data readiness at least medium

RENEGOTIATE_RUN_COST.action: renegotiate the AI running cost with the vendor (volume tier, commitment discount)
RENEGOTIATE_RUN_COST.expected_test: net annual benefit > 0 at the quoted price

UNCOMPETITIVE_COST.action: re-quote or re-scope: the AI costs more per unit than the work it replaces

OVER_BUDGET.action: phase the rollout or move it to the next budget cycle
OVER_BUDGET.expected_test: budget status within or at risk

DATA_NOT_READY.action: fill the missing inputs (stated run cost, adoption, baseline, overlap group)

BASELINE_MISSING.action: record today's cost of the process (volume, minutes per unit, loaded hourly cost)
BASELINE_MISSING.expected_test: baseline cost known; retained human cost computed

NO_CLEAR_WINNER.action: run the top contenders as limited pilots side by side and decide on observed adoption
NO_CLEAR_WINNER.expected_test: score gap above the margin after measurement

proposal_states.recommended: in the funded set (section-2 rule: highest total net within budget)
proposal_states.viable: passes every eligibility gate but is not funded (budget or overlap)
proposal_states.not_viable: fails at least one mandatory eligibility gate

view_rules.chart_sync: every chart lists proposals in `series_order` (funding rank, then the rest) so colours and selection stay in step across the four charts
view_rules.yearly_rule: monthly engine flows summed into 12-month years; the sum of yearly net equals profit_inr

formulas.cash_flow_t: benefit × ramp(t) − running cost(t); one-time cost in month 1
formulas.breakeven_month: first month where cumulative cash flow ≥ 0
formulas.profit_loss: Σ cash flows over the horizon
formulas.ai_run_cost: monthly tokens × 12 × price per 1M ÷ 1,000,000 + fixed annual
formulas.next_fy_cost: tokens × (1 + usage growth) and price × (1 + price drift); fixed annual unchanged
formulas.token_value: (net annual savings ÷ annual tokens in millions) ÷ price per 1M tokens
formulas.inflation_flag: usage growth ≥ 0 carries AI spend into the next FY
formulas.gross_cost_avoidance: typed annual benefit, or baseline cost × automation share
formulas.cashable_savings: gross × cashable share (default: the benefit type's cash factor)
formulas.retained_human_cost: baseline cost − gross (unknown without a baseline)
formulas.weighted_score: Σ weight × criterion normalised 0-100 across the compared set
formulas.risk_adjusted_value: net annual × readiness factor (low 0.6 / medium 0.8 / high 1.0)
formulas.evidence_band: weighted share of decision-driving inputs that are observed or calculated (real user data); ≥ 0.75 high, ≥ 0.40 medium, else low; fixture (synthetic) money values cap the band at Low
